# Python entry points

The functions and classes a script calls most. Each page is its docstring: parameters, return value, a runnable example and related entry points. Before 1.0 the Python API may change between minor versions; each such change has a changelog line. See the [Python API guide](../../python-api.md) for how they fit together.

| Entry point | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`nagasim.api.run_model`](run_model.md) |  |
| [`nagasim.experiments.run_scenarios`](run_scenarios.md) | Run every named scenario (all of them by default) and return the results. |
| [`nagasim.experiments.run_until_precision`](run_until_precision.md) | Keep adding replications until the confidence interval on a KPI is tight enough. |
| [`nagasim.experiments.suggest_warmup`](suggest_warmup.md) | Suggest a warm-up length from a run's entity log with MSER-5. |
| [`nagasim.experiments.flatten_kpis`](flatten_kpis.md) | Flatten the scalar KPI frames of a results dict into one long table. |
| [`nagasim.optimize.optimize`](optimize.md) | Search the factor space for the best response within a replication budget. |
| [`nagasim.calibrate.calibrate`](calibrate.md) | Tune factors until the model reproduces observed targets. |
| [`nagasim.forecast.forecast`](forecast.md) | Run a short terminating horizon from the system's current state. |
| [`nagasim.inputfit.best_fit`](best_fit.md) | Fit candidate distributions to a sample and return the winner. |
| [`nagasim.modelcheck.assert_model`](assert_model.md) | Assert, in a test, that a model passes its own assertions, reality and path checks. |
| [`nagasim.modelschema.build_json_schema`](build_json_schema.md) | Return the current model file format as a draft 2020-12 JSON Schema. |
| [`nagasim.build.Model`](Model.md) | A model written in Python; the file it produces is the model. |
| [`nagasim.results.Results`](Results.md) | What a run returns: KPI frames by name, with notebook conveniences. |
| [`nagasim.build.export_python`](export_python.md) | Return builder code for a model. |
| [`nagasim.modelfmt.minimal`](minimal.md) | Return the shortest form of a model that migrates to the same model. |
| [`nagasim.core.document.ModelDocument`](ModelDocument.md) | An in-memory model, edited only through this API. |
| [`nagasim.core.session.SimSession`](SimSession.md) | One replication of a model, driven from outside in chunks. |
| [`nagasim.rl.SimEnv`](SimEnv.md) | One RL episode = one replication of *layout*, paused at every decision of *policy*. Gymnasium-shaped but does not require gymnasium installed. |
| [`nagasim.laws.checks`](checks.md) | Every computable law and guardrail for one run (see the module docstring). |
| [`nagasim.state.take`](take.md) | The state document of *layout* at model time *at* of the run with *seed*. |
| [`nagasim.state.start`](start.md) | The model with a state document's state as its `initial_state`. |
| [`nagasim.uncertainty.input_uncertainty`](input_uncertainty.md) | Each KPI's run-to-run interval, its interval with the inputs' uncertainty, and the inputs' share of the spread. |
| [`nagasim.uncertainty.input_uncertainty_frame`](input_uncertainty_frame.md) | Each KPI's run-to-run interval, its interval with the inputs' uncertainty, and the inputs' share of the spread, as a DataFrame with one row per KPI. |
| [`nagasim.twin.forecast_from_state`](forecast_from_state.md) | The default runner: *horizon* from the clock the model's state starts at. |
| [`nagasim.twin.read_result`](read_result.md) | The latest result a twin wrote into *directory*. |
| [`nagasim.investment.investment_case`](investment_case.md) | One row per scenario of *result*, the baseline first (COLUMNS). |
| [`nagasim.appearance.look_of`](look_of.md) | Provisional. Everything needed to draw one conveyor piece: each look field of its type, resolved. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.exit_openings`](exit_openings.md) | Provisional. The gaps a piece's side exits cut in its guides, which the file never stores. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.material`](material.md) | Provisional. The material that one look value paints, as the reference drawing draws it. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.forms_of`](forms_of.md) | Provisional. The form and drawn size of every entity type in a model. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.piece_start`](piece_start.md) | Provisional. Where a conveyor piece starts on the floor: its position and heading. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.piece_segments`](piece_segments.md) | Provisional. A conveyor piece's path as straight and arc segments, in metres. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.piece_pose`](piece_pose.md) | Provisional. The pose on a conveyor piece's centreline at a distance along its path. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.piece_length_m`](piece_length_m.md) | Provisional. A conveyor piece's length along its path, in metres. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.length_factor`](length_factor.md) | Provisional. Metres per length unit of one conveyor piece. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.guide_runs`](guide_runs.md) | Provisional. The stretches of one side guide that stand: [0, *length*] minus that side's openings. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.guide_material`](guide_material.md) | Provisional. The material of a piece's side guides; use it rather than the raw `MATERIALS` entry. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.fields_of`](fields_of.md) | Provisional. The look fields a conveyor type takes, in the order an editor lists them. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.default`](default.md) | Provisional. The value of a look field that a piece does not set. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.srgb`](srgb.md) | Provisional. The sRGB channels of a colour `#RRGGBB`, each 0 to 1. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.linear_rgb`](linear_rgb.md) | Provisional. sRGB channels to linear ones, as a glTF base colour takes them. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.is_hex`](is_hex.md) | Provisional. Whether *value* is a colour `#RRGGBB`: six hex digits, either case, nothing around them. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.form_of`](form_of.md) | Provisional. The form one entity type draws as, from its name and icon; one of `FORMS`. |
| [`nagasim.appearance.default_carton_size`](default_carton_size.md) | Provisional. The size of a carton whose type declares none, in metres (length, width, height). |
